items.title: Lionel Ferbos Interview, 1964-08-03
items.q: No, you remember when you were- Moro. Yeah, that's right. Moro. Uh-huh.

ctx.x: Client and piano and the greatest, one of the greatest alto players that ever put an alto

to his mouth. No, no, no. I don't want you. You never met him? Just unassumable as can be, but the finest play you ever play? He never smiled. He's a phenomenal. I'm a smart guy. He's a nice fellow. And even one of the fun times we would have, in fact I would have so many different times I wouldn't know exactly when we'd stop working on that because it'd be one place and there'd be another. We'd work at the, what was it, the Papaw? Oh, Decatur Street. Yeah. Papaw and Decatur Street. We worked at the Lake,…

One thing I was going to ask you, it depends. You know, that band you were talking about with Son Johnson, that was at the Entertainers Club. That was after the band you had with Johnny Handy. Yeah. That's right.
